traits.note: FNA vol. 27, Grimmia (Hastings and Greven; efloras, read 2026-11-05): plants 5-40(-70) mm, in dense cushions to loose mats, olivaceous to dark black-green; muticous to long-awned, awns rarely longer than the blade; seta straight or arcuate; capsule erect. The typical values are the commonest Grimmia of walls and roofs, G. pulvinata (same volume): hemispherical hoary grey-green cushions, stems 1-3 cm, leaves 1-1.7 x 0.3-0.6 mm, flexuose when dry and erect when moist, abruptly narrowed to a short to long awn; seta arcuate 3-4 mm; capsule usually present, exserted, ellipsoid, brownish; on acid to basic rock, old mortar and tree trunks. Wikipedia, Grimmia pulvinata (read 2026-11-05): cushions 1-2 cm tall.

traits.capsule_length_m.note: FNA gives no capsule length for G. pulvinata; about its leaf's length, as drawn in floras' plates of the species. Check against a measured flora.

traits.capsule_colour.note: FNA vol. 27, Grimmia pulvinata (read 2026-11-05): capsule brownish when empty and dry.

traits.capsule_share.note: FNA vol. 27, Grimmia pulvinata (read 2026-11-05): capsules usually present, its cushions easily known by their abundant capsules; autoicous. The share is of shoots, not of cushions: a cushion of some hundreds of shoots bears tens of capsules. Our reading of 'usually present' and 'abundant'.

traits.hair_point_length_m.note: FNA vol. 27, Grimmia pulvinata (read 2026-11-05): short to long awn. Wikipedia and the UBC bryophyte pages (as summarised in a search, read 2026-11-05): the hair-point a third to a half of the leaf, at times as long as it. Typical about half the leaf.

traits.leaf_colour.note: Olive grey-green, as FNA's 'olivaceous' and 'grayish green' (Grimmiaceae, G. pulvinata); the grey of the cushion comes from the hyaline awns, drawn separately. Hue measured: imagekit run moss-colour-2026-11-05 on batch moss-pnw-2026-11-05 (iNaturalist research-grade photos from Washington, about 20 a taxon, script moss_colour.py): the median linear r/g and b/g of the moss pixels (G. pulvinata r/g 0.81, b/g 0.34). Photos are exposed brighter than moss is, so only the hue is taken from them; the brightness is a green reflectance of 0.13, a lit leaf's, just above the 0.05-0.11 moss canopies reflect in the visible (Lovelock and Robinson 2002, Plant Cell Environ. 25: 1239, Antarctic Grimmia; moss biocrust albedo about 0.11 against 0.20 for bare soil, Sci. Total Environ. 2020), the canopy's own shade darkening the shell further.

traits.colony_spread_m_per_year.note: Estimate: a G. pulvinata cushion reaches 2 to 4 cm across over one to two decades on a wall top. To check against Glime, Bryophyte Ecology, vol. 1, chapter 5 (growth).

traits.operculum_form.note: FNA vol. 27, Grimmia pulvinata: operculum rostrate. (efloras, read 2026-11-05)
